name: Ragi (Finger Millet)
blurb: The forgiving crop of the Deccan. Tolerates poor soil and patchy rain, and the government buys it at a guaranteed price.
beginner: Hardy, cheap to grow, almost impossible to fail completely. The best first crop in southern Karnataka.
plan: Plough twice, spread 4 tonnes farmyard manure per acre, level the field.
Raise seedlings for 4 weeks in a small bed, or broadcast-sow 4 kg seed in lines.
Move 25-30 day seedlings: 25 cm between rows, 10 cm between plants.
Hand-weed and give 20 kg urea per acre as top dressing.
Light weeding. Watch for leaf blast: diamond-shaped grey spots.
Keep soil moist. Bird scaring helps from here.
Cut earheads when they turn brown, dry 3 days, thresh, store at 12% moisture.

name: Maize (Hybrid)
blurb: The workhorse of Karnataka. Poultry-feed demand keeps buyers lined up at every APMC.
beginner: Reliable and easy to mechanise. The main risk is fall armyworm, which is simple to control if you scout early.
plan: Plough, harrow, add 4 tonnes manure. Make ridges 60 cm apart.
Dibble 1 seed per hill, 20 cm apart. Treat seed before sowing.
Apply 25 kg urea per acre; earth-up the rows.
Check leaf whorls twice weekly for caterpillars and frass; treat early.
Second 25 kg urea before tasselling. Do not let the field dry out.
Irrigation is critical at silking and grain filling.
Harvest when husks dry and grain moisture is 20-25%. Dry to 14% before selling.

name: Groundnut
blurb: A cash oilseed that also fixes nitrogen and leaves the soil better than it found it.
beginner: Loose red sandy soil is ideal. Pod harvest is labour-heavy but the price per quintal is strong.
plan: Fine tilth is vital. Apply 2 tonnes manure and 100 kg gypsum per acre.
Treat kernels with Rhizobium and Trichoderma. Sow 5 cm deep.
Apply 200 kg gypsum per acre for pod filling. Scout for leaf spot.
Keep soil moist and loose so pegs can enter. Do not let it crust.
Pull a plant: the inner shell shows dark veins and the kernel fills the pod.
Lift plants, strip pods, sun-dry to 8% moisture. Store dry to avoid aflatoxin.

name: Tur (Pigeon Pea)
blurb: A deep-rooted pulse with some of the best returns per rupee for dry land. Pairs well as an intercrop.
beginner: Low investment and almost no irrigation. Patience is the price: five months to harvest.
plan: One deep ploughing, then harrow. Add 2 tonnes manure.
Sow after the first good monsoon rain. Treat seed with Rhizobium.
Thin to one plant every 30 cm. Weed twice in the first 8 weeks.
Pinch growing tips at 40 days to encourage branching.
Scout for pod borer. Install 5 pheromone traps per acre.
Spray neem seed extract (5%) if pod borer is above threshold.
Harvest when 80% of pods turn brown. Sun-dry, thresh, clean.

name: Bengal Gram (Chickpea)
blurb: Grows on stored soil moisture after the monsoon. Cheap to raise and the government buys it.
beginner: The rabi crop that needs almost no water. Best on the black soils of north Karnataka.
plan: Plough after the rains end, keep the moisture. Apply 2 tonnes manure.
Sow in Oct-Nov at 8-10 cm depth. Treat seed with Trichoderma against wilt.
One light irrigation if available. Nip tips at 30-35 days.
Pheromone traps; spray HaNPV or neem if needed.
Harvest when leaves turn yellow and drop. Dry 3-4 days, thresh.

name: Jowar (Sorghum)
blurb: The rabi jowar of north Karnataka: a staple with built-in demand, and fodder as a second income.
beginner: Lowest cost crop here. Stalks sell as fodder, so one field pays you twice.
plan: Plough and harrow. Rabi jowar relies on stored moisture, so preserve it.
Thin to 15 cm spacing, one inter-cultivation.
20 kg urea per acre if moisture allows.
Look for dead hearts in young plants; remove and burn.
Harvest earheads when grain is hard. Cut and stack stalks for fodder.

name: Paddy (Rice)
blurb: Dependable price floor thanks to MSP procurement. Needs standing water, so only for assured irrigation or canal command.
beginner: Procurement makes income predictable, but water and labour needs are high.
plan: Sow 24 kg treated seed in a 1/10th acre nursery bed.
Plough in standing water, level, add 4 tonnes manure.
Plant 21-25 day seedlings, 2 per hill, 20 x 15 cm.
Weed, give 30 kg urea. Keep 2-3 cm water.
Second urea dose. Watch for blast and stem borer.
Keep field wet. Drain 10 days before harvest.
Harvest at 80% golden grains. Dry to 14% moisture.

name: Cotton (Bt Hybrid)
blurb: Strong gross income on black soil, but heavy on labour, pests and cash. Not a first-timer crop.
beginner: Held back for beginners because pest management is demanding.
plan: Dibble sow with the first monsoon rains, 2 seeds per hill.
Thin to 1 plant per hill. Weed twice before 60 days.
NPK split application; spray for sucking pests.
Scout weekly for pink bollworm and whitefly.
Pick fully burst bolls in the morning, keep clean.
Three to four pickings. Destroy stalks afterwards to break the pest cycle.

name: Onion
blurb: Big upside when prices spike, a real chance of loss when they crash. Price swings are the whole story.
beginner: High reward, high variance. Never put more than a third of your land in it in year one.
plan: Sow 4 kg seed in raised beds for 45-day seedlings.
Fine tilth, flat beds. Transplant 15 x 10 cm.
Weed twice; split 40 kg N through the crop.
Reduce nitrogen. Watch for purple blotch and thrips.
Lift when tops fall. Cure in shade for 5-7 days before storage or sale.

name: Tomato
blurb: Can pay for a whole year in one season, and can wipe you out in a week of price crash or leaf-curl virus.
beginner: Left out of beginner plans on purpose. Capital-heavy, staking, and constant disease management.
plan: Raise in a protected tray nursery for 25 days.
Stake and plant 90 x 45 cm on raised beds with mulch.
Tie plants every week. Prune suckers.
Weekly scouting for leaf curl, early blight and fruit borer.
Pick at breaker stage; sort and grade.
Pick every 3 days and send to market promptly.

name: Sunflower
blurb: Short-duration oilseed. Excellent price per quintal and the lowest cultivation cost among oilseeds.
beginner: Short, cheap, high price. Bees matter, so avoid spraying during flowering.
plan: Sow 1 seed per hill 3-4 cm deep. Soak seed overnight.
Thin to one plant, one weeding.
20 kg urea; irrigate at button stage.
Brush heads by hand if bees are scarce. A boron spray helps seed set.
Harvest when the back of the head turns lemon-yellow to brown.

name: Green Gram (Moong)
blurb: Ready in 70 days, so you are paid before most farmers finish weeding. Also improves the soil.
beginner: The safest start: fast, cheap, minimal inputs, and it leaves nitrogen behind for the next crop.
plan: One ploughing and harrow. 1 tonne manure.
Treat seed with Rhizobium. Sow 3 cm deep.
Scout for yellow mosaic virus; rogue out infected plants.
Dry and thresh. Turn the residue into the soil.

name: Sugarcane
blurb: Fixed FRP price from factories and a ratoon second crop, but it needs a full year of heavy water.
beginner: Only if you have canal or abundant borewell water and can wait 12 months for income.
plan: Deep plough, 10 tonnes manure, make furrows 4 ft apart.
Plant 2-3 bud setts after a fungicide dip.
Cut at 12 months; supply to the factory within 24 hours.

name: Turmeric
blurb: High-value spice with huge margins in good years, but heavy capital and nine months of work.
beginner: A year-two crop. Seed rhizomes alone cost over a lakh per acre.
plan: Plant finger rhizomes 5 cm deep, mulch.
Scout for leaf blotch and rhizome rot.
Leaves dry and yellow at 7-9 months.
Dig, boil, dry and polish rhizomes.
